transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I've barely been sleeping. It started after a warehouse inspection I did for work recently. I just lie there at night replaying bits of it in my head. And when I do manage to drift off, I wake up sweating and completely wide awake... it feels like I'm right back near that blast.
How long ago did this warehouse inspection incident happen?
It was about a week ago. That's when the explosion happened during my inspection. So, yeah, this has all been going on for about a week now, ever since that day.
Aside from nighttime, have you been having any sudden, vivid memories or flashbacks of the explosion during the day, or find yourself avoiding things that remind you of it?

Yeah, I do get them during the day. I'll just be sitting at work, reviewing a policy or... or looking at a loss report, and suddenly I'll get hit with this really sharp image of the worker on the floor and the soot in the air. It just happens out of nowhere, and it feels like my body reacts to it before I can even stop it.
Have you noticed yourself avoiding certain places, activities, or conversations that remind you of the explosion, like specific work sites or types of inspections?

Yeah, I have. I've actually been completely avoiding the file for that specific warehouse. And... well, I've also started letting any calls about other industrial accounts just go straight to voicemail. Honestly, even just the thought of opening emails related to those types of inspections makes my stomach drop, so I've just been steering clear of them as much as I can.
Since the explosion, have you noticed yourself feeling unusually on edge or jumpy, like being easily startled by sudden noises or feeling like you need to constantly watch out for danger?

Yeah, I've been really jumpy. It's... it's honestly exhausting. Just being at the office, every time a printer jams loudly, or a door slams somewhere down the hall, or even if someone just walks up behind my desk to ask a question... I jump. And not just a little flinch, I jump like something terrible is about to happen. My heart starts racing, and it takes me several minutes to just breathe and settle back down. It's like I can't turn off that feeling of being on edge.

Since the explosion, have you noticed times where you feel detached from yourself or your surroundings, like you're in a daze, watching things happen from outside your body, or like things around you don't feel real?

No, I don't think I've felt anything like that. I've definitely been on edge and having those sudden memories, but I haven't felt like I'm outside my body or in a daze. Everything feels pretty real, just... really overwhelming sometimes. But no, not detached.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating at work or on daily tasks since the explosion?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with my concentration. I mean, I'm definitely avoiding certain tasks, like I mentioned before, but when I actually sit down to do the work I *can* do, I'm able to focus on it fine. It's just the stuff that reminds me of the explosion that's the problem.
Have you noticed any trouble remembering important details of what happened during the explosion, like gaps in your memory of the event?

Yeah, actually, I have. I can clearly remember hearing the explosion... and then I can remember standing outside afterward with soot on my jacket. But the part in between is just completely blank. I mean, no matter how hard I try to piece it together, I just can't remember how I got from the building to the outside. It's just missing.
